reading.body:
Alteryx provides analytics automation software that integrates AI for data blending and self-service analytics, positioning itself in the data preparation layer rather than model development or inference.

The distinction matters for AI infrastructure. Data quality and preparation consume significant engineering effort before any model sees input, yet the compute requirements here are modest compared to training or deployment. Alteryx sits upstream of the inference path, automating the human work of structuring raw data into usable form. This belongs to the broader stack, but it is not where compute constraints tighten.

The data covers a single product line and does not specify deployment scale, customer base, infrastructure needs, or power consumption. It identifies what Alteryx does, not the resource requirements that would connect it to the binding constraints on AI scaling. The category label "Data & Analytics AI" is broad enough that the actual role in any particular AI project—whether critical or peripheral—remains unclear from this entry alone.

profile_text.body:
Alteryx is a data analytics and automation company, founded in 2011 and headquartered in Irvine. Its site describes it as "the agentic analytics and automation company" that helps organizations turn complex data into trusted insights, decisions, and action through AI-ready datasets, governed business logic, and visual workflows. The company's main offering described on the site is Alteryx One, which it says automates data workflows, reduces manual work, and delivers insights faster, and which integrates with Snowflake, Databricks, and BI tools.

On AI, Alteryx positions its products around trust and governance rather than model development. The site says every workflow Alteryx One produces is visible, understandable, repeatable, and auditable, a set of properties it abbreviates as VURA, and that agents created by Alteryx One inherit the same foundation. It claims users can "100X your decision making" by turning trusted data into decisions with automated business logic, low-code tools, AI assistance, and built-in governance. The company also says it is rated a leader across multiple 2026 analyst evaluations for making advanced analytics and AI trustworthy at enterprise scale, and cites McLaren Racing as a customer using Alteryx AI data analytics for on-track and off-track data. Named people on the site include CEO Andy MacMillan, MIT's Dr. Barb Wixom, Steve Nouri, Nezrin Noushad, and Anthony Alteirac.

The product tracked for Alteryx is Alteryx AI, in the data and analytics AI category, covering analytics automation with AI, data blending, and workflow governance, with self-service analytics risk noted. No litigation, MCP servers, SEC filings, or patent facts are recorded for the company.
